institution: National Academy of Music 'Prof. Pancho Vladigerov' (Национална музикална академия „Проф. Панчо Владигеров“, NMA)
program: Звукорежисура, звуков и медиен дизайн (Sound Engineering, Sound and Media Design) — TWO-YEAR master's track
qualification: ОКС „магистър“ (Master's, second cycle). Two variants: 1-year (only for holders of a BA in the same specialty) and 2-year (for holders of a degree in a DIFFERENT specialty).
accreditationStatus: State higher education institution, accredited by NEAA (Bulgarian National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency); founded 1921; only dedicated music university in Bulgaria.
language: BULGARIAN ONLY — no English track. Handbook states verbatim: 'За чужденците се изисква да владеят български език' (Foreigners are required to know Bulgarian), proven by (1) a document from a Bulgarian HEI, (2) passing a written+oral Bulgarian exam before a commission appointed by the Rector, or (3) completing a one-year preparatory language course at NMA.
durationEcts: 2 academic years (4 semesters) for the non-cognate route; 1 year for cognate BA holders. ECTS UNVERIFIED (Bulgarian norm 120 ECTS for 2-year master's).
whatYouStudy: Sound engineering, sound and media design; per the entrance interview syllabus the field covers physical acoustics, electroacoustic transducers, mixing consoles, amplifiers, processors, spatial audio formats, and 'Компютърни и електронни музикални технологии' (computer and electronic music technologies).
entryRequirements: Bachelor's or master's degree from any recognised HEI. Foreign diplomas must first pass NMA's recognition procedure: 'Кандидатите – българи и чужденци, които притежават диплома за висше образование, издадена от чуждестранно висше училище, се допускат до приемни изпити след като преминат успешно процедурата за признаване на придобито висше образование в чужбина' — and these recognition papers must be filed with the Учебен отдел in the PRECEDING academic year and at least TWO MONTHS before the application documents. Minimum grade for admission to fee-paying master's study: Добър 4.00 on the entrance exam; 4.50 on each exam to compete for state-funded (държавна поръчка) places.
acceptsNonMusic: YES — and this is the single most important finding for this candidate. The 2-year master's is explicitly designed for non-cognate degrees: 'двугодишната магистратура е по специалност, която е различна от специалността в дипломата за „бакалавър“'. Crucially, unlike Композиция, Музикознание and all Дирижиране tracks — which each carry the line 'Необходимо е кандидатът да притежава музикална образователно-квалификационна степен „Бакалавър“' (the candidate must hold a MUSIC bachelor's degree) — the two Звукорежисура tracks carry NO such clause. A software-engineering BSc is therefore not excluded on paper.
portfolioSpec: NO PORTFOLIO REQUIRED for the 2-year Звукорежисура track. The entrance requirement is an interview only. (By contrast the 2-year Композиция track requires 'представяне от кандидата пред комисията на собствени камерни или симфонични произведения на партитури' — presentation of the candidate's own chamber or symphonic works in score — i.e. notated scores, which this candidate does not have.)
auditionSpec: NO LIVE AUDITION, NO PERFORMANCE TEST. Entrance is a ТЕМИ ЗА СЪБЕСЕДВАНЕ (interview on set topics), quoted verbatim: '1. Физическа акустика - основни понятия. Поведение на звука в пространството. Звукови явления и закономерности. 2. Звукотехнически устройства - електроакустични преобразуватели, смесителни пултове, усилватели, процесори. 3. Пространствени звукови формати - характеристика, особености, приложение. 4. Компютърни и електронни музикални технологии – специфика и приложение.' Reading list is Ballou 'Handbook for Sound Engineers', Huber & Runstein 'Modern Recording Techniques', Huber 'The MIDI Manual', Eargle 'The Microphone Book' / 'Loudspeaker Handbook', Blackstock 'Fundamentals of Physical Acoustics'. This is an ENGINEERING interview, not a music audition — an unusually good match for a software-engineering graduate. BUT it must be conducted in Bulgarian.
tuitionNonEU: €8,500 per year. NMA's own English-language tuition page states verbatim: 'For a Master's degree – 8500 €'. NOT free and far above €3,000 — the Bulgarian domestic/state-subsidised rate does NOT apply to non-EU nationals.
otherFees: Application fee 100 BGN (~€51): 'Документ за платена такса за кандидатстване /100 лева/'. Plus costs of the foreign-diploma recognition procedure and of the one-year Bulgarian preparatory language course if taken (amount UNVERIFIED).
totalCostEstimate: ~€17,000 tuition over 2 years + ~€500–700/month living in Sofia (~€6,000–8,000/yr) + preparatory Bulgarian year if needed. Realistically €30,000+ over the full path. Only viable with a bilateral scholarship.
scholarshipName: Bulgarian Government bilateral scholarships for foreign nationals (administered by the Bulgarian Ministry of Education and Science via Bulgarian diplomatic missions, under bilateral cultural/educational agreements)
scholarships: UNVERIFIED whether Tunisia currently has an active quota. Bulgaria awards places to foreign nationals under bilateral agreements and under Decree 103/1993; applications normally go through the Bulgarian embassy accredited to Tunisia. Amounts and deadline UNVERIFIED — must be confirmed with the Bulgarian embassy. Note: state-funded (държавна поръчка) places at NMA are competed for on the same entrance exams but availability to non-EU nationals is UNVERIFIED.
languageRequirement: Bulgarian, at a level certified either by a Bulgarian HEI document or by passing NMA's own written+oral Bulgarian exam; otherwise a compulsory one-year preparatory language year.
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2025/26): documents 27 May – 4 June 2025; exams 5–21 June 2025; ranking 23 June 2025; enrolment 24–26 June 2025. Foreign-diploma recognition papers must be filed a full academic year earlier. Expect an equivalent late-May/early-June 2027 window for September 2027 entry. Separately, non-EU applicants under the state ordinance file 1–30 June and 1–15 September in the year of application.
applicationOpens: Late May (state-funded June session). PRIOR CYCLE dates above; 2027 dates not yet published.

institution: National Academy of Music 'Prof. Pancho Vladigerov' (NMA)
program: Звукорежисура и звуков дизайн за игри (Sound Engineering and Sound Design for Games) — TWO-YEAR master's track
qualification: ОКС „магистър“ (Master's, second cycle), 1 or 2 academic years; 2-year route for non-cognate bachelor's degrees.
language: BULGARIAN ONLY. Same rule: 'За чужденците се изисква да владеят български език'.
durationEcts: 2 years for non-cognate entrants (4 semesters). ECTS UNVERIFIED.
whatYouStudy: Game audio: sound engineering and sound design for interactive media/games. Interview syllabus identical to the media-design track (acoustics, audio hardware, spatial audio formats, computer and electronic music technologies).
entryRequirements: Same as the sister track: any bachelor's/master's degree; foreign diplomas require NMA's recognition procedure filed a year in advance; minimum 4.00 (paid) / 4.50 (state-funded) on the entrance exam.
acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — no 'must hold a music bachelor's' clause appears for this specialty in the 2025/26 handbook, and the 2-year variant is expressly for a different specialty from the bachelor's diploma.
auditionSpec: NO AUDITION. Interview on the same four technical topics (physical acoustics; audio devices; spatial sound formats; computer and electronic music technologies) with the same engineering reading list. In Bulgarian.
otherFees: 100 BGN application fee (~€51); diploma-recognition procedure costs UNVERIFIED.
scholarshipName: Bulgarian Government bilateral scholarships (Ministry of Education and Science, via Bulgarian embassies)
scholarships: UNVERIFIED for Tunisia — confirm with the Bulgarian embassy accredited to Tunis. Amount and deadline UNVERIFIED.
languageRequirement: Bulgarian (certificate, NMA exam, or one-year preparatory course).
deadline: PRIOR CYCLE (2025/26): 27 May – 4 June 2025 documents; 5–21 June 2025 exams. 2027 dates unpublished.

institution: National Academy of Music 'Prof. Pancho Vladigerov' (NMA)
whatYouStudy: Art composition (concert/classical tradition). No electroacoustic or computer-music specialisation is named in the handbook.
entryRequirements: VERBATIM: 'VI. Специалност „Композиция“ - срок на обучение две години. Необходимо е кандидатът да притежава музикална образователно-квалификационна степен „Бакалавър“' — the candidate MUST hold a MUSIC bachelor's degree.
acceptsNonMusic: NO — explicitly excluded. Music bachelor's degree mandatory.
portfolioSpec: VERBATIM: 'представяне от кандидата пред комисията на собствени камерни или симфонични произведения на партитури' — the candidate presents their own chamber or symphonic works IN SCORE. Notated scores only; no provision for audio/DAW work.
auditionSpec: Portfolio presentation before the commission + 'събеседване с комисията' (interview with the commission). In Bulgarian.
_verdict: RULED OUT for this candidate — music BA mandatory and score portfolio required.

institution: New Bulgarian University (Нов български университет, NBU) — Department of Music
qualification: магистър по тонрежисура (Master in Sound Engineering), second cycle. NBU's e-catalogue lists the current (2026) version as a 2-semester programme.
accreditationStatus: Private but state-recognised and NEAA-accredited university (founded 1991); Department of Music is an AEC (Association Européenne des Conservatoires) member.
language: BULGARIAN. The e-catalogue entry for Тонрежисура gives the language as Bulgarian. NBU does run English-taught master's programmes, but within the Music Department only 'Музикално изпълнителство / Musical Performance' is offered in English — NOT the sound-engineering track. Confirm directly with foreign.student@nbu.bg.
durationEcts: 2 semesters (1 year) in the 2026 catalogue version; 60 ECTS implied by the course-credit table (12 + 6 + 15 + 30 ECTS structure listed). Longer 'non-cognate' variants may exist — UNVERIFIED.
whatYouStudy: VERBATIM (Bulgarian): specialised training in 'тонрежисура, звукови технологии, софтуерни решения в музикалното студио, електронен звук, звуков монтаж, аудиодизайн на звук, синтез на звук, мастеринг, звук в киното и телевизията, компютърно моделиране на звуковата картина' — sound engineering, audio technologies, software solutions in the music studio, electronic sound, sound editing, sound design, sound synthesis, mastering, sound in film and TV, computer modelling of the sound image. Graduates are qualified as sound engineers, audio designers, sound operators, music arrangers and 'композитори на електронна музика' (electronic music composers).
entryRequirements: Bachelor's or master's degree. NBU's international page states for non-EU applicants: 'Non-EU citizens, holders of a degree, apply by submitting relevant documents' — i.e. document-based admission, whereas 'EU applicants attend an interview or an exam, submit a motivation essay, and meet any additional requirements set by the specific program.' Any programme-specific specialised exam (специализиран изпит) for this MA is UNVERIFIED — the music department page references one but details it only for bachelor's applicants.
acceptsNonMusic: LIKELY YES — no music-degree prerequisite is stated, and NBU's non-EU admission route is document-based. NOT explicitly confirmed on an official page — treat as UNVERIFIED and confirm with the department (mkrusteva@nbu.bg).
portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — no portfolio specification published on the accessible programme pages.
auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED. For non-EU applicants NBU's own wording implies NO interview/exam ('apply by submitting relevant documents'), with the interview/exam route described for EU applicants. This is unusually low-barrier if confirmed. Must be verified with the department in writing.
tuitionNonEU: €5,521.95 – €6,749.05 per year. NBU's official English fees page states verbatim for master's programmes other than Architecture and Law: '10 800 - 13 200 BGN / 5521.95 - 6749.05 EUR (per year)'. The exact figure for Тонрежисура is UNVERIFIED — NBU says fees vary by programme; confirm at foreign.student@nbu.bg. WELL ABOVE €3,000.
otherFees: Bachelor's-level entrance testing fee is quoted as '40 лева / 20,45 евро'; master's application fee UNVERIFIED. Non-EU students pay tuition annually rather than per semester.
scholarshipName: NBU internal tuition discounts (UNVERIFIED for non-EU) / Bulgarian Government bilateral scholarships
scholarships: UNVERIFIED. No published non-EU scholarship scheme found on NBU's international pages.
languageRequirement: Bulgarian for this programme (UNVERIFIED whether any English delivery is possible on request).
deadline: UNVERIFIED — NBU's international pages reference a 'Key dates and deadlines' page but the accessible content gives no dates. NBU generally runs rolling admissions for international students with a main September intake.

institution: New Bulgarian University (NBU) — Department of Music
program: Музикално продуцентство (Music Production), MA — and the historical 'Тонрежисура и компютърна музика' (Sound Engineering and Computer Music) MA
whatYouStudy: Music production / music industry; the sister title 'Тонрежисура и компютърна музика' covers sound engineering plus computer music. NOTE: these two titles appear in NBU's e-catalogue under older academic years (2013), so CURRENT AVAILABILITY IS UNVERIFIED. The department's own current listing names only 'Тонрежисура' among the audio tracks.
tuitionNonEU: If running, the same non-EU band applies: 10,800–13,200 BGN / €5,521.95–€6,749.05 per year.
_verdict: MAY NO LONGER EXIST — verify before counting on it.

institution: University of Zagreb — Academy of Dramatic Art (Akademija dramske umjetnosti, ADU), Department of Editing (Odsjek montaže)
program: Oblikovanje zvuka (Sound Design) — sveučilišni diplomski studij (graduate university study), a module of the Montaža master's
qualification: Sveučilišni magistar / magistra (graduate university degree), second cycle.
accreditationStatus: Constituent of the University of Zagreb (public); ADU founded 1950; accredited by the Croatian Agency for Science and Higher Education.
language: CROATIAN. No English-taught version found. ADU publishes exclusively in Croatian and the entrance exam materials are in Croatian.
durationEcts: UNVERIFIED on the official programme page (Croatian graduate norm: 2 years / 120 ECTS).
whatYouStudy: VERBATIM (goal): 'obrazovanje kreativnih, ali i stručnih profesionalnih djelatnika' — training creative and technically skilled professionals who acquire knowledge of sound across film, television, radio and the performing arts. Sound design for picture, sound post-production, sound dramaturgy. This is FILM/MEDIA sound craft, not electronic music composition.
entryRequirements: Completed undergraduate programme, plus either direct-admission status or passing the entrance exam's elimination threshold, ranked on a priority list until the quota is filled. The graduate quota is split between the Montaža and Oblikovanje zvuka directions 3:3, exceptionally 4:2 or 2:4 — i.e. only about THREE places per year in sound design.
acceptsNonMusic: Not stated as restricted to any bachelor's field — the requirement is a completed undergraduate degree plus the entrance exam. NOT explicitly confirmed for non-arts degrees; treat as UNVERIFIED. In practice the portfolio requirement (an existing audiovisual work with the candidate's own sound design) is the real filter.
portfolioSpec: VERBATIM (paraphrased from the department regulation): candidates must submit (1) an audiovisual work in which they conceived or co-created the sound image ('audiovizualni rad u kojem je pristupnik osmislio ili sudjelovao u stvaranju zvučne slike'), in DVD-video format, at least 3 copies; and (2) a written analysis of that audiovisual work explaining the sound concept and the sources of sounds, music, sound effects and the computer programs used in sound post-production — three copies. NOTE: this requires a finished AV work with the candidate's own sound design; a music-only portfolio would not satisfy it.
auditionSpec: ENTRANCE EXAM (prijamni ispit) with an elimination threshold, not a live music audition. The exam is built around the submitted AV work and its written analysis; the call publishes annually 'application deadlines, entrance works, exam procedures, scoring methods, passing score, consultations, direct-enrolment rights'. The call for the graduate programme is announced about 3 months and at least one month before classes begin.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED. Croatian law places third-country nationals in a separate foreigners' quota and the fee is 'prescribed by the institution itself' — ADU has not published a figure that could be located. Croatian public-university master's fees for internationals generally run up to about €4,000/yr, and University of Zagreb rates cited in secondary sources are €2,000–€5,000/yr, but NO OFFICIAL ADU NUMBER WAS FOUND. Do not assume the Croatian domestic subsidised rate.
scholarshipName: Croatian Government Scholarships for foreign nationals (administered by the Agency for Mobility and EU Programmes / Ministry of Science, Education and Youth, under bilateral agreements)
scholarships: UNVERIFIED whether Tunisia holds an active bilateral quota; amounts and deadlines UNVERIFIED.
languageRequirement: Croatian — level UNVERIFIED but the entrance exam and teaching are in Croatian.
deadline: UNVERIFIED for 2027. Call published annually, roughly 3 months before term start (so around June for an October start).
_verdict: Very small intake (~3 places), Croatian-language, portfolio requires a finished AV work. Weak fit.

institution: University of Zagreb — Academy of Music (Muzička akademija Sveučilišta u Zagrebu)
qualification: NOT A STANDALONE SECOND-CYCLE DEGREE. FLAGGED: composition at Zagreb is an 'integrirani preddiplomski i diplomski sveučilišni studij' — an INTEGRATED 5-year undergraduate+graduate programme. There is no separate 2-year master's entry point, so a graduate holding a foreign BSc cannot enter at master's level; entry is at year 1 of a 5-year course.
accreditationStatus: Public; constituent of the University of Zagreb; largest and oldest higher music institution in Croatia (est. 1829, re-established 1921); AEC member.
durationEcts: 5 years integrated (300 ECTS) — not a 120-ECTS master's.
whatYouStudy: In the electronic-composition specialisation: Electronic Music Techniques, Fundamentals of Electronic Music, Applied Music Techniques, Harmony, Polyphony, Musical Forms and Styles, Aspects of Contemporary Music, Music Informatics, Solfège; plus compulsory Piano, Conducting, Score Reading and Music History. Heavily classical-conservatoire in framing despite the electronic label.
entryRequirements: Entrance to year 1 of the integrated study via the Academy's razredbeni (entrance) procedure — classical musicianship exams (solfège, harmony, piano) plus composition portfolio. Full spec UNVERIFIED.
acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice — the integrated study assumes secondary music-school preparation (solfège, piano, harmony). Not stated verbatim; treat the formal wording as UNVERIFIED but the structure rules this out.
auditionSpec: Live entrance exam (razredbeni ispit) including musicianship tests — UNVERIFIED exact spec.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — third-country students enrol under a foreigners' quota and pay a fee set by the institution. No published figure found.
scholarshipName: Croatian Government Scholarships for foreign nationals (bilateral)
_verdict: RULED OUT — not a master's degree; integrated 5-year study only.

institution: University of Split — Arts Academy (Umjetnička akademija u Splitu, UMAS), Music Department
program: Glazbena teorija i Kompozicija (Music Theory and Composition), sveučilišni diplomski studij
qualification: Sveučilišni magistar (graduate university degree), second cycle.
accreditationStatus: Public; constituent of the University of Split.
durationEcts: Graduate study following a 240-ECTS, 8-semester undergraduate degree. Duration/ECTS of the graduate stage UNVERIFIED (Croatian norm 2 years / 120 ECTS).
whatYouStudy: Composition and music theory in the classical/concert tradition. No electronic-music or production content advertised.
entryRequirements: VERBATIM: 'završen prijediplomski studij u trajanju od 8 semestara (240 ECTS bodova)' plus a passed final exam. Ranking out of 100 points: 'prosjek ocjena tijekom prijediplomskog studija – maksimalno 10 bodova' and 'rezultati razredbenog postupka – maksimalno 90 bodova'; pass mark 'najmanje 55 bodova'. NOTE: requires a 240-ECTS/4-year bachelor's — a 3-year 180-ECTS BSc would not meet this on its face.
acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice. The composition entrance requires eight original compositions plus three instrumental arrangement tasks; the music-theory track requires a 3.50 undergraduate GPA plus dictation and analysis exams. Not stated as open to non-music degrees — treat as effectively closed.
portfolioSpec: For Composition: submission of EIGHT original compositions meeting specified instrumentation requirements, plus three instrumental arrangement assignments, plus an oral examination on the presented works. Scores expected.
auditionSpec: YES — a razredbeni (entrance) procedure worth 90 of 100 points. For Music Theory it includes single-line dictation with alterations and modulations, three-voice dictation, sight-singing with frequent key changes, formal-harmonic analysis of Romantic works and formal-tonal analysis of polyphonic works. For Composition, an oral exam on the submitted works. Hard classical-musicianship gate.
_verdict: RULED OUT — eight original scored compositions + classical musicianship exams + 240-ECTS bachelor's requirement.

institution: Josip Juraj Strossmayer University of Osijek — Academy of Arts and Culture (Akademija za umjetnost i kulturu u Osijeku, UAOS)
program: Diplomski sveučilišni studij Kompozicija (Composition) — also Teorija muzike (Music Theory)
qualification: Sveučilišni magistar, second cycle (diplomski sveučilišni studij).
accreditationStatus: Public; constituent of the University of Osijek.
durationEcts: UNVERIFIED (not published on the accessible programme list).
whatYouStudy: Composition with music theory. The Academy's own material notes graduates gain 'competency in music management and production' and that the Composition-with-Music-Theory route is recommended for those aiming to work as a music producer — but this is framed around acoustic/classical composition, not electronic music.
entryRequirements: UNVERIFIED — the graduate programme list page publishes no admission detail. The cognate undergraduate is 'Kompozicija s teorijom muzike'.
auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — a razredbeni postupak is standard at Croatian arts academies; spec not published.

institution: University of Pécs (Pécsi Tudományegyetem, PTE) — Faculty of Music and Visual Arts, Department of Electronic Music and Media Art (Elektronikus Zenei és Média Tanszék)
qualification: Mesterképzés / MA (second cycle). Established 2020 as the continuation of the existing Electronic Music and Media Art BA.
accreditationStatus: Public state university; PTE's Faculty of Music and Visual Arts is the only higher-education centre in Hungary integrating music and fine-arts training in one faculty (est. 1996). Programme accredited 2020.
language: HUNGARIAN ONLY. The programme page gives it as a 2-year full-time programme taught in Hungarian, and it does NOT appear on PTE's English-taught 'Music and Arts' study-programme list (which contains only Classical Music Performance MA, Choir Conducting MA, Ceramics Design MA, Classical Singing MA and the Electronic Music and Media Art BA). This is the single biggest obstacle — the content is otherwise close to ideal.
durationEcts: 2 years (4 semesters), 120 ECTS. Official credit split: theory/history/culture 14; creative-research work 12; design and artistic practice 48; electives 10; professional internship 6; thesis and diploma work 30.
whatYouStudy: 'Artistic forms which use sound as primary medium or material' — sound installation, multimedia performance, sonic experimentation, and interdisciplinary work at the intersection of music, visual art, media studies, humanities and sciences. Grew directly out of the Electronic Music and Media Art BA, whose stated field is 'sound, noise, silence and their electronic / digital forms', sound art, interactive arts, networked projects and performative arts. This is a genuine electroacoustic / sound-art department, not a classical conservatoire.
entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree or higher university qualification; 'strong computer-based artistic knowledge (especially music-related)'; demonstrated interest in sound-art creation and research. VERBATIM (Hungarian): 'olyan, BA szakot vagy magasabb szintű egyetemi képzést végzett hallgatókat tud fogadni, akik komplex számítógépes művészeti (különösen zenei) ismeretekkel rendelkeznek' — it can admit students who have completed a BA or higher who possess complex COMPUTER-BASED artistic (especially musical) knowledge.
acceptsNonMusic: STRONG YES on the face of it — no music degree is required. The stated prerequisite is a bachelor's of any kind plus 'complex computer-based artistic (especially musical) knowledge'. For a software-engineering graduate with a self-built electronic-music practice this is one of the most favourable admission clauses found anywhere in the region. NOT stated verbatim as 'we accept non-music degrees' — treat the wording above as the evidence.
portfolioSpec: Required submissions: (1) an ELECTRONIC PORTFOLIO documenting previous work; (2) a DETAILED WORK PLAN with timeline, bibliography and anticipated publications. No scores, no notation requirement — DAW/electronic work is the expected medium.
auditionSpec: NO LIVE MUSIC AUDITION. The entrance examination is: (1) a PRACTICAL EXAM worth max 34 points — presentation of the portfolio and work plan; (2) an ORAL EXAM worth max 15 points — discussion plus ON-SITE MULTIMEDIA CREATIVE PROBLEM-SOLVING. Maximum 49 points, doubled to a 100-point scale under institutional regulations. Note the on-site component implies physical attendance in Pécs — remote option UNVERIFIED.
tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED for this specific programme. PTE's English-taught arts master's (e.g. Classical Singing MA) are cited at €3,000 per semester (€6,000/yr) for both EU and non-EU students — but Hangművészet is a Hungarian-language programme, for which the self-financed fee is UNVERIFIED and may be much lower. Confirm with international@pte.hu. FREE if won via Stipendium Hungaricum.
otherFees: UNVERIFIED (Hungarian universities typically charge a ~€100–200 application/processing fee for self-financed international applicants).
totalCostEstimate: €0 tuition + full stipend if Stipendium Hungaricum is won; otherwise UNVERIFIED tuition + ~€500–600/month living in Pécs (one of the cheapest university cities in Hungary).
scholarships: Stipendium Hungaricum is fully funded: complete tuition-fee waiver, monthly stipend, dormitory/housing contribution and medical insurance. TUNISIA IS AN ELIGIBLE TERRITORY — Tunisia appears explicitly in the accepted-citizenship list on Hungarian DreamApply course pages verified during this sweep. DEADLINE for the 2026/27 round: 15 January 2026 (application on Tempus Public Foundation's DreamApply platform); expect an equivalent mid-January 2027 deadline for September 2027 entry. CRITICAL CAVEAT: it is UNVERIFIED whether Hangművészet MA is listed in the Stipendium Hungaricum catalogue — Hungarian-taught programmes are sometimes offered with a one-year preparatory Hungarian language year, sometimes not offered at all. This must be checked in the SH course finder when the 2027 catalogue opens (roughly November 2026).
languageRequirement: Hungarian — level UNVERIFIED; the entrance exam (oral exam plus on-site problem-solving) is conducted in Hungarian.
deadline: UNVERIFIED for the Hungarian-language route (Hungarian national admissions via felvi.hu normally close 15 February for the autumn intake). Stipendium Hungaricum deadline 15 January (2026/27 round).
applicationOpens: SH catalogue typically opens November; Hungarian national admission opens ~January.
_verdict: CONTENT-WISE THE BEST MATCH IN HUNGARY — a real sound-art MA that expects computer-based rather than conservatoire skills, with a portfolio-and-work-plan entrance instead of a live audition. Blocked only by the Hungarian language of instruction. High priority to verify SH eligibility and whether any English accommodation is possible.

institution: Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design (MOME)
qualification: Master of Arts, full degree, second cycle.
accreditationStatus: Public (state-recognised) art and design university; English-language IxD MA launched 2021; listed in the Stipendium Hungaricum catalogue.
language: ENGLISH-TAUGHT — verbatim: 'International students are welcome; all teaching is in English.'
durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years). ECTS not stated on the SH course page — UNVERIFIED (Hungarian MA norm 120 ECTS).
whatYouStudy: Interaction design: digital products and services, prototyping, user-centred design process, critical reflection on technology's role in society. NOT a sound or music programme — included here because MOME was on the review list and because it is the one MOME MA whose admission wording explicitly welcomes a technology bachelor's. Sound work would only be possible as self-directed project content.
entryRequirements: Bachelor diploma (or higher): 'BAhons / BA in Arts / BSc'. All BA certificates undergo an equivalency protocol conducted by MOME with the recommendation of the Hungarian National Equivalency and Information Office; foreign BA certificates must be equivalent to a Hungarian bachelor certificate. Original BA degree certificate must be presented at enrolment.
acceptsNonMusic: YES, EXPLICITLY. VERBATIM: 'Who can apply? Applicants with a BA in design, technology, media, communication, or any related field that connects to Interaction Design. ... No professional work experience required. Curiosity, creativity, and a portfolio that shows your thinking are what matter.' A BSc in software engineering falls squarely inside 'technology'.
portfolioSpec: VERBATIM: 'A relevant portfolio is required. Portfolios must be uploaded to the Tempus Public Foundation's DreamApply interface together with the application documents. ... Case studies that show digital product work (apps, websites, prototypes). - No professional projects yet? No problem — include schoolwork, redesigns, or fictional projects. - Show awareness of the user-centered design process: its steps and how you apply them. - Include personal work that shows your background: studies, essays, code, research, or craft. - Show your creative side — design is problem-solving. Let us see how you do it. - Links to prototypes or videos are welcome, but your portfolio should also make sense without them. - Recommended length: 10–50 pages. Multiple projects are encouraged.' Note it explicitly accepts CODE as portfolio evidence.
auditionSpec: NO AUDITION. 'Portfolios will be reviewed by a committee of our professors. Based on the portfolio selection applicant may be invited for an ONLINE INTERVIEW in April.' Remote interview — no travel required at the admission stage.
tuitionNonEU: €12,000 PER SEMESTER for non-EEA citizens (€24,000/yr) on the self-financed route — MOME's own tuition page gives EEA citizens EUR 5,000/semester and non-EEA citizens EUR 12,000/semester. FAR above €3,000/yr. Only realistic via Stipendium Hungaricum (100% waiver) or MOME's own tuition-fee support.
totalCostEstimate: €48,000 over 2 years self-financed; €0 tuition on Stipendium Hungaricum.
scholarshipName: Stipendium Hungaricum (plus MOME's own tuition-fee support for international students)
scholarships: Stipendium Hungaricum: full tuition waiver + monthly stipend + accommodation contribution + medical insurance. TUNISIA IS ON THE ACCEPTED-CITIZENSHIP LIST for this exact course (verified on the DreamApply course page). SH deadline 15 January (2026/27 round). MOME's own process: applications completed during February–March, portfolio selection after nomination at end of March, admission interviews mid-April. MOME separately offers tuition-fee support to accepted international students from specified regions based on professional accomplishments (amount UNVERIFIED).
languageRequirement: English. VERBATIM: 'Applicants are not required to present an English language certificate, however a minimum B2, preferably higher-C1 level knowledge of English is necessary. Applicants' language proficiency will be evaluated and assessed during the admission process and at the entry examination interview.'
englishTest: NONE REQUIRED — no IELTS/TOEFL certificate demanded; assessed at interview. This is a notable advantage.
deadline: Stipendium Hungaricum: 15 January (2026/27 round; 2027/28 date not yet published). MOME's own admission steps run February–April.
applicationOpens: SH catalogue opens ~November; MOME portfolio requirements published from November.
_verdict: NOT field A or B — it is interaction design, not sound. Included as an adjacent, unusually accessible English-taught, fully-fundable option for a software engineer with no music credentials. MOME's other English MAs (Animation, Photography, Designer-Maker, Design, Art and Design Management) contain no sound/music track.

institution: University of Theatre and Film Arts (Színház- és Filmművészeti Egyetem, SZFE)
program: Hangmester (film sound engineer) — SPECIALISATION OF THE BA, NOT A MASTER'S
qualification: FLAGGED — NOT A SECOND-CYCLE DEGREE. 'Mozgókép – hangmester szakirány' is a specialisation within SZFE's undergraduate (BA) motion-picture programme, historically run in class cohorts (e.g. 2007–2010, 2019–2022). No standalone MA in sound engineering or sound design was found in SZFE's mesterképzés (master's) listing.
accreditationStatus: Public state university (Hungary's national theatre and film school).
language: Hungarian for the sound specialisation. SZFE does participate in one 4-semester ENGLISH-language Erasmus Mundus joint master's delivered with Universidade Lusófona (Portugal) and LUCA School of Arts Brussels (Belgium) — but that is a film/creative-practice degree, not a sound degree.
durationEcts: BA specialisation — not applicable as a master's.
whatYouStudy: Film and television sound recording, sound editing and mixing (at BA level).
entryRequirements: BA-level entry via SZFE's multi-round talent examination — not open as a master's entry point.
scholarships: UNVERIFIED whether SZFE lists any programme relevant to sound in the SH catalogue.
_verdict: RULED OUT — no master's-level sound programme at SZFE. NOT A SECOND-CYCLE DEGREE.
